The rest either did not belong to such an organization, or there was no information available about them.[[120]](#cite_note-121) The largest religious denomination recorded in 2010 was the [Protestant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant "Protestant") [regional church body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landeskirche "Landeskirche")—the [Evangelical Church of Berlin-Brandenburg-Silesian Upper Lusatia (EKBO)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelical_Church_of_Berlin-Brandenburg-Silesian_Upper_Lusatia "Evangelical Church of Berlin-Brandenburg-Silesian Upper Lusatia")—a [united church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_church "United church"). EKBO is a member of the [Protestant Church in Germany (EKD)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant_Church_in_Germany "Protestant Church in Germany") and of the [Union of Protestant Churches in the EKD (UEK)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_of_Protestant_Churches_in_the_EKD "Union of Protestant Churches in the EKD"). According to the EKBO, their membership accounted for 19% of the local population, while the [Roman Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") had 9% of residents registered as its members.[[121]](#cite_note-122) About 3% of the population identify with other Christian denominations (mostly [Eastern Orthodox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church "Eastern Orthodox Church"), but also various Protestants).[[122]](#cite_note-Amt_für_Statistik_Berlin–Brandenburg-2010-123) According to the Berlin residents register, in 2018 15% were members of the Evangelical Church, and 9% were members of the Catholic Church.[[102]](#cite_note-Amt_für_Statistik_Berlin-Brandenburg-103) The government keeps a register of members of these churches for tax purposes, because it collects [church tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_tax#Germany "Church tax") on behalf of the churches. It does not keep records of members of other religious organizations which may collect their own church tax, in this way. In 2009, approximately 249,000 [Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim "Muslim") were reported by the [Office of Statistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amt_für_Statistik_Berlin-Brandenburg "Amt für Statistik Berlin-Brandenburg") to be members of mosques and Islamic religious organizations in Berlin,[[123]](#cite_note-124) while in 2016, the newspaper *[Der Tagesspiegel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Der_Tagesspiegel "Der Tagesspiegel")* estimated that about 350,000 Muslims observed [Ramadan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramadan "Ramadan") in Berlin.[[124]](#cite_note-Ramadan-125) In 2019, about 437,000 registered residents, 12% of the total, reported having a [migration background](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Migration_background "Migration background") from one of the [Member states of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_states_of_the_Organization_of_Islamic_Cooperation "Member states of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation").[[102]](#cite_note-Amt_für_Statistik_Berlin-Brandenburg-103)[[124]](#cite_note-Ramadan-125) Between 1992 and 2011 the Muslim population almost doubled.[[125]](#cite_note-126) About 1% of Berliners belong to other religions. Of the estimated population of 30,000–45,000 Jewish residents,[[126]](#cite_note-127) approximately 12,000 are registered members of religious organizations.[[122]](#cite_note-Amt_für_Statistik_Berlin–Brandenburg-2010-123) Berlin is the seat of the [Roman Catholic archbishop of Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Archdiocese_of_Berlin "Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Berlin") and [EKBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelical_Church_of_Berlin-Brandenburg-Silesian_Upper_Lusatia "Evangelical Church of Berlin-Brandenburg-Silesian Upper Lusatia")'s elected chairperson is titled the bishop of EKBO. Furthermore, Berlin is the seat of many Orthodox cathedrals, such as the Cathedral of St. Boris the Baptist, one of the two seats of the [Bulgarian Orthodox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgarian_Orthodox_Church "Bulgarian Orthodox Church") Diocese of Western and Central Europe, and the Resurrection of Christ Cathedral of the Diocese of Berlin (Patriarchate of Moscow). The faithful of the different religions and denominations maintain many [places of worship in Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_places_of_worship_in_Berlin "List of places of worship in Berlin"). The [Independent Evangelical Lutheran Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Evangelical_Lutheran_Church "Independent Evangelical Lutheran Church") has 8 parishes of different sizes in Berlin.[[127]](#cite_note-128) There are 36 [Baptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptist "Baptist") congregations (within [Union of Evangelical Free Church Congregations in Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_of_Evangelical_Free_Church_Congregations_in_Germany "Union of Evangelical Free Church Congregations in Germany")), 29 [New Apostolic Churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Apostolic_Church "New Apostolic Church"), 15 [United Methodist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Methodist "United Methodist") churches, 8 Free Evangelical Congregations, four [Churches of Christ, Scientist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_Christ,_Scientist "Church of Christ, Scientist") (1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 11th), 6 congregations of [the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter-day_Saints "The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints"), an [Old Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Catholic "Old Catholic") church, and an [Anglican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglican "Anglican") church in Berlin. Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Police "Berlin Police") ### City state [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: City state")] Since [German reunification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_reunification "German reunification") on 3 October 1990, Berlin has been one of the three [city-states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City-states "City-states") among the present 16 [states of Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_of_Germany "States of Germany"). The [Abgeordnetenhaus von Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abgeordnetenhaus_von_Berlin "Abgeordnetenhaus von Berlin") (*House of Representatives*) functions as the city and state parliament, which has 141 seats. Berlin's executive body is the [Senate of Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_of_Berlin "Senate of Berlin") (*Senat von Berlin*). The Senate consists of the [Governing Mayor of Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governing_Mayor_of_Berlin "Governing Mayor of Berlin") (*Regierender Bürgermeister*), and up to ten senators holding ministerial positions, two of them holding the title of "Mayor" (*Bürgermeister*) as deputy to the Governing Mayor.[[130]](#cite_note-131) The total annual budget of Berlin in 2015 exceeded €24.5 ($30) billion including a budget surplus of €205 ($240) million.[[131]](#cite_note-132) The state of Berlin owns extensive assets, including administrative and government buildings, real estate companies, as well as stakes in the Olympic Stadium, swimming pools, housing companies, and numerous public enterprises and subsidiary companies.[[132]](#cite_note-133)[[133]](#cite_note-134) The state of Berlin runs a real estate portal to advertise commercial spaces or land suitable for redevelopment.[[134]](#cite_note-135) The [Social Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Democratic_Party_of_Germany "Social Democratic Party of Germany") (SPD) and [The Left](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Left_(Germany) "The Left (Germany)") (Die Linke) took control of the city government after the [2001 state election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_state_election,_2001 "Berlin state election, 2001") and won another term in the [2006 state election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_state_election,_2006 "Berlin state election, 2006").[[135]](#cite_note-136) From the [2016 state election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_state_election,_2016 "Berlin state election, 2016") until the [2023 state election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Berlin_state_election "2023 Berlin state election"), there was a coalition between the Social Democratic Party, the Greens and the Left Party. Since April 2023, the government has been formed by a coalition between the Christian Democrats and the Social Democrats.[[136]](#cite_note-Kai_Wegner_zum_Regierenden_Bürgermeister_von_Berlin_gewählt-2023-137) The Governing Mayor is simultaneously Lord Mayor of the City of Berlin (*Oberbürgermeister der Stadt*) and Minister President of the State of Berlin (*Ministerpräsident des Bundeslandes*). The office of the Governing Mayor is in the [Rotes Rathaus (Red City Hall)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotes_Rathaus "Rotes Rathaus"). Since 2023, this office has been held by [Kai Wegner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kai_Wegner "Kai Wegner") of the Christian Democrats.[[136]](#cite_note-Kai_Wegner_zum_Regierenden_Bürgermeister_von_Berlin_gewählt-2023-137) He is the first conservative mayor in Berlin in more than two decades.[[137]](#cite_note-138) * Main article: [Boroughs and neighborhoods of Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boroughs_and_neighborhoods_of_Berlin "Boroughs and neighborhoods of Berlin") [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Berlin_Subdivisions.svg/330px-Berlin_Subdivisions.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Berlin_Subdivisions.svg) [Berlin's 12 boroughs and their 96 neighborhoods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boroughs_and_neighborhoods_of_Berlin "Boroughs and neighborhoods of Berlin") Berlin is subdivided into 12 boroughs or districts (*Bezirke*). Each borough has several subdistricts or neighborhoods (*Ortsteile*), which have roots in much older municipalities that predate the formation of Greater Berlin on 1 October 1920. These subdistricts became urbanized and incorporated into the city later on. Many residents strongly identify with their neighborhoods, colloquially called *[Kiez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiez "Kiez")*. At present, Berlin consists of 96 subdistricts, which are commonly made up of several smaller residential areas or quarters.[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Each borough is governed by a borough council (*Bezirksamt*) consisting of five councilors (*Bezirksstadträte*) including the borough's mayor (*Bezirksbürgermeister*). The council is elected by the borough assembly (*Bezirksverordnetenversammlung*). However, the individual boroughs are not independent municipalities, but subordinate to the Senate of Berlin.[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] The borough's mayors make up the council of mayors (*Rat der Bürgermeister*), which is led by the city's Governing Mayor and advises the Senate. The neighborhoods have no local government bodies. ### City partnerships [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: City partnerships")] For a more comprehensive list, see [List of twin towns and sister cities in Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_twin_towns_and_sister_cities_in_Germany "List of twin towns and sister cities in Germany"). Berlin to this day maintains official partnerships with 17 cities.[[138]](#cite_note-139) [Town twinning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_city "Sister city") between [West Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Berlin "West Berlin") and other cities began with its sister city Los Angeles, California, in 1967. [East Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Berlin "East Berlin")'s partnerships were canceled at the time of [German reunification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_reunification "German reunification"). ### Capital city [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Capital city")] Berlin is the capital of the Federal Republic of Germany. The [President of Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Germany "President of Germany"), whose functions are mainly ceremonial under the [German constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grundgesetz "Grundgesetz"), has their official residence in [Bellevue Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellevue_Palace_(Germany) "Bellevue Palace (Germany)").[[139]](#cite_note-140) Berlin is the [seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seat_of_government "Seat of government") of the [German Chancellor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chancellor_of_Germany_(1949–) "Chancellor of Germany (1949–)") (Bundeskanzler), housed in the [Chancellery building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Chancellery_(Berlin) "Federal Chancellery (Berlin)"), the *Bundeskanzleramt*. Facing the Chancellery is the [Bundestag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundestag "Bundestag"), the German Parliament, housed in the renovated [Reichstag building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reichstag_building "Reichstag building") since the government's relocation to Berlin in 1998. The [Bundesrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundesrat_of_Germany "Bundesrat of Germany") ("federal council", performing the function of an [upper house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_house "Upper house")) is the [representation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federalism "Federalism") of the [16 constituent states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_of_Germany "States of Germany") (*Länder*) of Germany and has its seat at the former [Prussian House of Lords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prussian_House_of_Lords "Prussian House of Lords"). The total annual federal budget managed by the German government exceeded €310 ($375) billion in 2013.[[140]](#cite_note-141) The relocation of the federal [government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Germany "Cabinet of Germany") and Bundestag to Berlin was mostly completed in 1999. However, some ministries, as well as some minor departments, stayed in the [federal city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_city "Federal city") [Bonn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonn "Bonn"), the former capital of West Germany. [Discussions about moving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin-Bonn_Act "Berlin-Bonn Act") the remaining ministries and departments to Berlin continue.[[141]](#cite_note-142) The [Federal Foreign Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Office_(Germany) "Foreign Office (Germany)") and the ministries and departments of [embassies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_diplomatic_missions_in_Germany#Diplomatic_missions_in_Berlin "List of diplomatic missions in Germany")[[142]](#cite_note-143) as well as the headquarters of many think tanks, trade unions, nonprofit organizations, lobbying groups, and professional associations. Frequent official visits and diplomatic consultations among governmental representatives and national leaders are common in contemporary Berlin. ## Economy [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Economy")] Main article: [Economy of Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Berlin "Economy of Berlin") In 2025, Berlin's GDP amounted to €218.3 billion and grew by 1.1% in real terms from the previous year. Between 2013 and 2025, Berlin's annual real GDP growth exceeded the national rate in every year, with the [service sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_sector "Service sector") providing the main contribution to growth.[[143]](#cite_note-144) Berlin's unemployment rate declined from its peak of 18.3% in 2005 to 7.8% in 2019. It rose during the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Germany "COVID-19 pandemic in Germany") and, after a temporary decline in 2022, increased to an annual average of 10.3% in 2025.[[144]](#cite_note-145) Important economic sectors in Berlin include life sciences, transportation, information and communication technologies, media and music, advertising and design, biotechnology, environmental services, construction, e-commerce, retail, hotel business, and medical engineering.[[145]](#cite_note-146) Research and development have economic significance for the city.[[146]](#cite_note-berlin.de-147) Several major corporations like [Volkswagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volkswagen "Volkswagen"), [Pfizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pfizer "Pfizer"), and [SAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAP "SAP") operate innovation laboratories in the city.[[147]](#cite_note-148) The Science and Business Park in Adlershof is the largest technology park in Germany measured by revenue.[[148]](#cite_note-149) Within the [eurozone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone "Eurozone"), Berlin has become a center for business relocation and international [investments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investment_(macroeconomics) "Investment (macroeconomics)").[[149]](#cite_note-150) ### Companies [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Companies")] [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/DBBuildingBerling150809.jpg/250px-DBBuildingBerling150809.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DBBuildingBerling150809.jpg) [Deutsche Bahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Bahn "Deutsche Bahn"), the largest railway company in the world,[[150]](#cite_note-Fortune-151) is headquartered in Berlin. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Berlin%2C_Mitte%2C_Behrenstrasse%2C_Berliner_Bank_05.jpg/250px-Berlin%2C_Mitte%2C_Behrenstrasse%2C_Berliner_Bank_05.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Berlin,_Mitte,_Behrenstrasse,_Berliner_Bank_05.jpg) [Deutscher Sparkassen- und Giroverband](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutscher_Sparkassen-_und_Giroverband "Deutscher Sparkassen- und Giroverband"), the European Union's second-largest financial services group, has its headquarters in Berlin. Many German and international companies have business or service centers in the city. For several years Berlin has been recognized as a major center of [business founders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrepreneurship "Entrepreneurship").[[151]](#cite_note-152) In 2015, Berlin generated the most venture capital for young [startup companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Startup_company "Startup company") in Europe.[[152]](#cite_note-153) Among the 10 largest employers in Berlin are the City-State of Berlin, [Deutsche Bahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Bahn "Deutsche Bahn"), largest railway company in the world,[[150]](#cite_note-Fortune-151) the hospital providers [Charité](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charité "Charité") and [Vivantes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivantes "Vivantes"), the Federal Government of Germany, the local public transport provider [BVG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berliner_Verkehrsbetriebe "Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe"), [Siemens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siemens "Siemens") and [Deutsche Telekom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Telekom "Deutsche Telekom").[[153]](#cite_note-154) Siemens, a [Global 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune_Global_500 "Fortune Global 500") and [DAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DAX "DAX")-listed company is partly headquartered in Berlin. Other DAX-listed companies headquartered in Berlin are the property company [Deutsche Wohnen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Wohnen "Deutsche Wohnen"), the online fashion retailer [Zalando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zalando "Zalando") and the online food delivery service [Delivery Hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delivery_Hero "Delivery Hero"). The national railway operator [Deutsche Bahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Bahn "Deutsche Bahn"),[[154]](#cite_note-155) Europe's largest digital publisher[[155]](#cite_note-156) [Axel Springer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axel_Springer_SE "Axel Springer SE") as well as the [MDAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MDAX "MDAX")-listed firm [HelloFresh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HelloFresh "HelloFresh") and also have their main headquarters in the city. Among the largest international corporations who have their German or European headquarters in Berlin are [Bombardier Transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombardier_Transportation "Bombardier Transportation"), [Securing Energy for Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Securing_Energy_for_Europe "Securing Energy for Europe"), [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola "Coca-Cola"), [Pfizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pfizer "Pfizer"), [Sony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony "Sony") and [TotalEnergies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TotalEnergies "TotalEnergies"). As of 2023, [Sparkassen-Finanzgruppe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparkassen-Finanzgruppe "Sparkassen-Finanzgruppe"), a network of [public banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_bank "Public bank") that together form the largest financial services group in Germany and in all of Europe, is headquartered in Berlin. The [Bundesverband der Deutschen Volksbanken und Raiffeisenbanken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundesverband_der_Deutschen_Volksbanken_und_Raiffeisenbanken "Bundesverband der Deutschen Volksbanken und Raiffeisenbanken") has its headquarters in Berlin, managing around 1.2 trillion euros.[[156]](#cite_note-157) The three largest banks in the capital are [Deutsche Kreditbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Kreditbank "Deutsche Kreditbank"), [Landesbank Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landesbank_Berlin "Landesbank Berlin") and [Berlin Hyp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Hyp "Berlin Hyp").[[157]](#cite_note-158) [Mercedes-Benz Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Group "Mercedes-Benz Group") manufactures cars, and [BMW builds motorcycles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_Motorrad "BMW Motorrad") in Berlin. In 2022, American electric car manufacturer [Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. "Tesla, Inc.") opened its first European Gigafactory outside the city borders in [Grünheide (Mark)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grünheide_(Mark) "Grünheide (Mark)"), Brandenburg. The Pharmaceuticals division of [Bayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayer "Bayer")[[158]](#cite_note-159) and [Berlin Chemie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Chemie "Berlin Chemie") are major pharmaceutical companies in the city. ### Tourism and conventions [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Tourism and conventions")] For a more comprehensive list, see [List of tourist attractions in Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tourist_attractions_in_Berlin "List of tourist attractions in Berlin"). Berlin had 788 hotels with 134,399 beds in 2014.[[159]](#cite_note-visitBerlin-160) The city recorded 28.7 million overnight hotel stays and 11.9 million hotel guests in 2014.[[159]](#cite_note-visitBerlin-160) Tourism figures have more than doubled within the last ten years and Berlin has become the 3rd-most-visited city destination in Europe. Some of the most visited places in Berlin include: [Potsdamer Platz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potsdamer_Platz "Potsdamer Platz"), [Brandenburger Tor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandenburg_Gate "Brandenburg Gate"), [the Berlin wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Wall "Berlin Wall"), [Alexanderplatz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexanderplatz "Alexanderplatz"), [Museumsinsel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_Island "Museum Island"), [Fernsehturm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernsehturm_Berlin "Fernsehturm Berlin"), the [East-Side Gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Side_Gallery "East Side Gallery"), [Schloss-Charlottenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlottenburg_Palace "Charlottenburg Palace"), [Zoologischer Garten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Zoological_Garden "Berlin Zoological Garden"), [Siegessäule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Victory_Column "Berlin Victory Column"), [Gedenkstätte Berliner Mauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gedenkstätte_Berliner_Mauer "Gedenkstätte Berliner Mauer"), [Mauerpark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauerpark "Mauerpark"), [Botanical Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin-Dahlem_Botanical_Garden_and_Botanical_Museum "Berlin-Dahlem Botanical Garden and Botanical Museum"), [Französischer Dom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Cathedral,_Berlin "French Cathedral, Berlin"), [Deutscher Dom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutscher_Dom "Deutscher Dom") and [Holocaust-Mahnmal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_to_the_Murdered_Jews_of_Europe "Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe"). The largest visitor groups are from Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Italy, Spain and the United States.[[160]](#cite_note-161) According to figures from the [International Congress and Convention Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Congress_and_Convention_Association "International Congress and Convention Association") in 2015, Berlin became the leading organizer of conferences globally, hosting 195 international meetings.[[161]](#cite_note-162) Some of these congress events take place on venues such as CityCube Berlin or the Berlin Congress Center (bcc). The [Messe Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messe_Berlin "Messe Berlin") (also known as Berlin ExpoCenter City) is the main convention organizing company in the city. Its main exhibition area covers more than 160,000 square meters (1,722,226 sq ft). Several large-scale trade fairs like the consumer electronics trade fair [IFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFA_Berlin "IFA Berlin"), where the first practical audio [tape recorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetophon "Magnetophon") and the first [completely electronic television system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manfred_von_Ardenne "Manfred von Ardenne") were first introduced to the public,[[162]](#cite_note-163)[[163]](#cite_note-164)[[164]](#cite_note-165)[[165]](#cite_note-166) the [ILA Berlin Air Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ILA_Berlin_Air_Show "ILA Berlin Air Show"), the [Berlin Fashion Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Fashion_Week "Berlin Fashion Week") (including the *Premium Berlin* and the *Panorama Berlin*),[[166]](#cite_note-167) the [Green Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_International_Green_Week "Berlin International Green Week"), the *Fruit Logistica*, the transport fair [InnoTrans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/InnoTrans "InnoTrans"), the tourism fair [ITB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITB_Berlin "ITB Berlin") and the adult entertainment and erotic fair [Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venus_Award "Venus Award") are held annually in the city, attracting a significant number of business visitors. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/Berlin_Fashion_Week_2013_b.jpg/250px-Berlin_Fashion_Week_2013_b.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Berlin_Fashion_Week_2013_b.jpg) [Berlin Fashion Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Fashion_Week "Berlin Fashion Week") [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/IFA_2012_IMG_7677.JPG/250px-IFA_2012_IMG_7677.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:IFA_2012_IMG_7677.JPG) [IFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internationale_Funkausstellung_Berlin "Internationale Funkausstellung Berlin") is one of Europe's leading trade shows for consumer electronics. ### Creative industries [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Creative industries")] For a more comprehensive list, see [List of films set in Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_films_set_in_Berlin "List of films set in Berlin"). [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/European_Film_Academy_-_European_Film_Awards_logo.svg/250px-European_Film_Academy_-_European_Film_Awards_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:European_Film_Academy_-_European_Film_Awards_logo.svg) The [European Film Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Film_Academy "European Film Academy") (logo pictured) was founded in Berlin. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Postfuhramt_%28Berlin%29_-msu-2021-4274-.jpg/250px-Postfuhramt_%28Berlin%29_-msu-2021-4274-.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Postfuhramt_(Berlin)_-msu-2021-4274-.jpg) [Postfuhramt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postfuhramt "Postfuhramt") in Berlin-Mitte, where [Ottomar Anschütz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottomar_Anschütz "Ottomar Anschütz") held the first showing of life sized pictures in motion on 25 November 1894[[167]](#cite_note-168) The [creative arts and entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_industries "Creative industries") business is an important part of Berlin's economy. The sector comprises music, film, advertising, architecture, art, design, [fashion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_fashion "German fashion"), performing arts, publishing, [R&D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_and_development "Research and development"), software,[[168]](#cite_note-169) TV, radio, and [video games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_gaming_in_Germany "Video gaming in Germany"). In 2014, around 30,500 creative companies operated in the Berlin-Brandenburg metropolitan region, predominantly [SMEs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_and_medium-sized_enterprises "Small and medium-sized enterprises"). Generating a revenue of 15.6 billion Euro and 6% of all private economic sales, the culture industry grew from 2009 to 2014 at an average rate of 5.5% per year.[[169]](#cite_note-170) Berlin is an important European and [German film industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_Germany "Cinema of Germany") hub.[[170]](#cite_note-171) It is home to more than 1,000 film and television production companies, 270 movie theaters, and around 300 national and international co-productions are filmed in the region every year.[[146]](#cite_note-berlin.de-147) The historic [Babelsberg Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babelsberg_Studios "Babelsberg Studios") and the production company [UFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universum_Film_AG "Universum Film AG") are adjacent to Berlin in [Potsdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potsdam "Potsdam"). The city is also home of the [German Film Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Filmakademie "Deutsche Filmakademie") (Deutsche Filmakademie), founded in 2003, and the [European Film Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Film_Academy "European Film Academy"), founded in 1988. ### Media [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Media")] Main article: [Media in Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Media_in_Berlin "Media in Berlin") Berlin is home to many magazine, newspaper, book, and scientific/academic publishers and their associated service industries. In addition, around 20 news agencies, more than 90 regional daily newspapers and their websites, as well as the Berlin offices of more than 22 national publications such as *[Der Spiegel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Der_Spiegel "Der Spiegel")*, and [Die Zeit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die_Zeit "Die Zeit") reinforce the capital's position as Germany's epicenter for influential debate. Therefore, many international journalists, bloggers, and writers live and work in the city.[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Berlin is the central location to several international and regional television and radio stations.[[171]](#cite_note-172) The public broadcaster [RBB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rundfunk_Berlin-Brandenburg "Rundfunk Berlin-Brandenburg") has its headquarters in Berlin as well as the commercial broadcasters [MTV Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe "MTV Europe") and [Welt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welt_(German_TV_channel) "Welt (German TV channel)"). German international public broadcaster [Deutsche Welle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Welle "Deutsche Welle") has its TV production unit in Berlin, and most national German broadcasters have a studio in the city, including [ZDF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZDF "ZDF") and [RTL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RTL_Television "RTL Television"). Berlin has Germany's largest number of daily newspapers, with numerous local [broadsheets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadsheet "Broadsheet") (*[Berliner Morgenpost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berliner_Morgenpost "Berliner Morgenpost")*, *[Berliner Zeitung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berliner_Zeitung "Berliner Zeitung")*, *[Der Tagesspiegel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Der_Tagesspiegel "Der Tagesspiegel")*), and three major [tabloids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabloid_(newspaper_format) "Tabloid (newspaper format)"), as well as national dailies of varying sizes, each with a different political affiliation, such as *[Die Welt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die_Welt "Die Welt")*, *[Neues Deutschland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neues_Deutschland "Neues Deutschland")*, and *[Die Tageszeitung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die_Tageszeitung "Die Tageszeitung")*. *[The Berliner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Berliner_(magazine) "The Berliner (magazine)")*, a monthly magazine, is Berlin's English-language periodical and [La Gazette de Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Gazette_de_Berlin "La Gazette de Berlin") a French-language newspaper.[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Berlin is also home to several major German-language publishing houses, including [Walter de Gruyter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_de_Gruyter "Walter de Gruyter"), [Springer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axel_Springer_AG "Axel Springer AG"), [Suhrkamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suhrkamp "Suhrkamp"), and [Cornelsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornelsen_Verlag "Cornelsen Verlag"). ## Quality of life [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Quality of life")] In a 2023 [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission") survey of 83 European cities, 86% of respondents in Berlin were satisfied with the city as a place to live. The survey also found that 83% were satisfied with their personal job situation.[[172]](#cite_note-173) In the 2025 [Global Power City Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_city#Global_Power_City_Index "Global city"), Berlin ranked fourth in the livability category among 48 cities. The category covers working conditions, the [cost of living](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cost_of_living "Cost of living"), safety, health and [well-being](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Well-being "Well-being"), and access to everyday services and amenities.[[173]](#cite_note-174) Berlin's 2025 Social Report, which covers developments through 2023, found that around 20% of residents were [at risk of poverty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_threshold "Poverty threshold"). It also found that a similar share of households spent at least 40% of their income on rent and associated charges.[[174]](#cite_note-175) ## Transport [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Transport")] Main article: [Transport in Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_in_Berlin "Transport in Berlin") ### Airports [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Airports")] [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/Berlin_Brandenburg_Airport_at_night.jpg/250px-Berlin_Brandenburg_Airport_at_night.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Berlin_Brandenburg_Airport_at_night.jpg) [Berlin Brandenburg Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Brandenburg_Airport "Berlin Brandenburg Airport") (BER) at night Berlin is served by one commercial international airport: [Berlin Brandenburg Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Brandenburg_Airport "Berlin Brandenburg Airport") (BER), located just outside Berlin's south-eastern border, in the state of Brandenburg. It began construction in 2006, with the intention of replacing [Tegel Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Tegel_Airport "Berlin Tegel Airport") (TXL) and [Schönefeld Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Schönefeld_Airport "Berlin Schönefeld Airport") (SXF) as the single commercial airport of Berlin.[[175]](#cite_note-176) Previously set to open in 2012, after extensive delays and cost overruns, it opened for commercial operations in October 2020.[[176]](#cite_note-177) The planned initial capacity of around 27 million passengers per year[[177]](#cite_note-178) is to be further developed to bring the terminal capacity to approximately 55 million per year by 2040.[[178]](#cite_note-179) Before the opening of the BER in Brandenburg, Berlin was served by Tegel Airport and Schönefeld Airport. Tegel Airport was within the city limits, and Schönefeld Airport was located at the same site as BER. Both airports together handled 30 million passengers in 2015. In 2014, 67 airlines served 163 destinations in 50 countries from Berlin.[[179]](#cite_note-180) Tegel Airport was a focus city for [Lufthansa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lufthansa "Lufthansa") and [Eurowings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurowings "Eurowings") while Schönefeld served as an important destination for airlines like [Germania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germania_(airline) "Germania (airline)"), [easyJet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EasyJet "EasyJet") and [Ryanair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryanair "Ryanair"). Until 2008, Berlin was also served by the smaller [Tempelhof Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempelhof_Airport "Tempelhof Airport"), which functioned as a city airport, with a convenient location near the city center, allowing for quick transit times between the central business district and the airport. The airport grounds have since been turned into a city park.[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] ### Roads [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Roads")] Berlin's transport infrastructure provides a diverse range of urban mobility.[[180]](#cite_note-181) A total of 979 bridges cross 197 km (122 miles) the inner-city waterways. Berlin roads total 5,422 km (3,369 miles) of which 77 km (48 miles) are motorways (known as [Autobahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autobahn "Autobahn")).[[181]](#cite_note-Amt_für_Statistik_Berlin_Brandenburg-182) In 2013 only 1.344 million motor vehicles were registered in the city.[[181]](#cite_note-Amt_für_Statistik_Berlin_Brandenburg-182) With 377 cars per 1000 residents in 2013 (570/1000 in Germany), Berlin as a Western global city has one of the lowest numbers of cars per capita.[[182]](#cite_note-183) ### Rail [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Rail")] [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Train_station_Berlin_Potsdamer_Platz.jpg/250px-Train_station_Berlin_Potsdamer_Platz.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Train_station_Berlin_Potsdamer_Platz.jpg) [DB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Bahn "Deutsche Bahn") [Station Potsdamer Platz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Potsdamer_Platz_station "Berlin Potsdamer Platz station") [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Berlin_Hauptbahnhof0514.JPG/250px-Berlin_Hauptbahnhof0514.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Berlin_Hauptbahnhof0514.JPG) [Berlin Hauptbahnhof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Hauptbahnhof "Berlin Hauptbahnhof") (Berlin Central Station) Long-distance rail lines directly connect Berlin with all of the major cities of Germany. The regional rail lines of the [Verkehrsverbund Berlin-Brandenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verkehrsverbund_Berlin-Brandenburg "Verkehrsverbund Berlin-Brandenburg") provide access to [Brandenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandenburg "Brandenburg") and to the [Baltic Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltic_Sea "Baltic Sea"). The [Berlin Hauptbahnhof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Hauptbahnhof "Berlin Hauptbahnhof") (Berlin Central Station) is the largest [grade-separated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grade_separation "Grade separation") railway station in Europe.[[183]](#cite_note-184) The [Deutsche Bahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Bahn "Deutsche Bahn") runs the high speed [Intercity-Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercity-Express "Intercity-Express") (ICE) to domestic destinations, including [Hamburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburg "Hamburg"), [Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich"), [Cologne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne "Cologne"), [Stuttgart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuttgart "Stuttgart"), and [Frankfurt am Main](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt_am_Main "Frankfurt am Main"). ### Water transport [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: Water transport")] The [Spree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spree_(river) "Spree (river)") and the [Havel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havel "Havel") rivers cross Berlin. There are no frequent passenger connections to and from Berlin by water. Berlin's largest inland port, the [Westhafen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westhafen "Westhafen"), is located in the district of [Moabit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moabit "Moabit"). It is a transhipment and storage site for inland shipping with a growing importance.[[184]](#cite_note-185) ### Intercity buses [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=35 "Edit section: Intercity buses")] There is an increasing quantity of [intercity bus services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercity_bus_service "Intercity bus service"). Berlin city has more than 10 stations[[185]](#cite_note-186) that run buses to destinations throughout Berlin. Destinations in Germany and Europe are connected via the intercity bus exchange *[Zentraler Omnibusbahnhof Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zentraler_Omnibusbahnhof_Berlin "Zentraler Omnibusbahnhof Berlin")*. ### Urban public transport [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=36 "Edit section: Urban public transport")] Heidelberger Platz station") The *[Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berliner_Verkehrsbetriebe "Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe")* (BVG) and the German State-owned [Deutsche was not served. Since 1989, the transport network has been developed extensively. However, it still contains early 20th century trains, such as the U1.[[187]](#cite_note-188) ### Cycling [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=37 "Edit section: Cycling")] Main article: [Cycling in Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling_in_Berlin "Cycling in Berlin") Berlin is well known for its highly developed [bicycle lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_lane "Bicycle lane") system.[[188]](#cite_note-189) It is estimated that Berlin has 710 bicycles per 1,000 residents. Around 500,000 daily bike riders accounted for 13% of total traffic in 2010.[[189]](#cite_note-190) Cyclists in Berlin have access to 620 km of bicycle paths including approximately 150 km of mandatory bicycle paths, 190 km of off-road bicycle routes, 60 km of bicycle lanes on roads, 70 km of shared bus lanes which are also open to cyclists, 100 km of combined pedestrian/bike paths and 50 km of marked bicycle lanes on roadside pavements or sidewalks.[[190]](#cite_note-191) Riders are allowed to carry their bicycles on [Regionalbahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regionalbahn "Regionalbahn") (RE), S-Bahn and U-Bahn trains, on trams, and on night buses if a bike ticket is purchased.[[191]](#cite_note-192) ### Taxicabs [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=38 "Edit section: Taxicabs")] Taxicabs in Berlin are yellow or beige. In 2024, around 8,000 [taxicabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxicabs "Taxicabs") were in service.[[192]](#cite_note-193) Like in most of Europe, app-based [sharing cab services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridesharing_company "Ridesharing company") are available but limited.[[193]](#cite_note-194) ## Energy [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=39 "Edit section: Energy")] [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Berlin-mitte_heizkraftwerk-mitte_20060605_629.jpg/250px-Berlin-mitte_heizkraftwerk-mitte_20060605_629.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Berlin-mitte_heizkraftwerk-mitte_20060605_629.jpg) Heizkraftwerk Mitte power plant Most of the electricity generated in Berlin comes from [combined heat and power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cogeneration "Cogeneration") (CHP) plants, which also supply the city's [district heating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_heating "District heating") networks. Berlin is a net importer of electricity and draws power from neighboring [Brandenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandenburg "Brandenburg"), particularly during summer, when local CHP plants operate at reduced output.[[194]](#cite_note-Berlin-electricity-2024-195) The [Berlin 380-kV electric line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_380-kV_electric_line "Berlin 380-kV electric line"), which crosses the city from Spandau to Marzahn, forms a central part of the city's transmission network.[[195]](#cite_note-196) Its connection to the regional grid in 1994 ended [West Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Berlin "West Berlin")'s operation as a power island.[[196]](#cite_note-197) [BEW Berliner Energie und Wärme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BEW_Berliner_Energie_und_Wärme?action=edit&redlink=1 "BEW Berliner Energie und Wärme (page does not exist)"), owned by the state of Berlin since 2024, operates several major CHP plants and the city's largest district heating network, which supplies about one third of Berlin's households.[[197]](#cite_note-BEW-public-ownership-198) Its largest plants are the coal-fired [Reuter West power station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuter_West_power_station?action=edit&redlink=1 "Reuter West power station (page does not exist)") and the natural gas-fired Berlin-Mitte power station.[[198]](#cite_note-BEW-generating-facilities-199) Electricity generation from [renewable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renewable_energy "Renewable energy") in the city is growing, driven particularly by [photovoltaics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photovoltaics "Photovoltaics"). By the end of 2025, Berlin had 55,861 photovoltaic installations with a combined capacity of 487 MWp. Their estimated annual generation was about 438 GWh, equivalent to approximately 6% of Berlin’s gross electricity generation.[[199]](#cite_note-200) Berlin's climate legislation requires the Senate to work toward a [phase-out of hard coal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coal_phase-out "Coal phase-out") by 2030.[[200]](#cite_note-Berlin-coal-phase-out-201) ## Health [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=40 "Edit section: Health")] [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Charit%C3%A9_vom_Futurium_aus.jpg/250px-Charit%C3%A9_vom_Futurium_aus.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Charité_vom_Futurium_aus.jpg) [Charité](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charité "Charité"), Europe's [largest university hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_hospitals_by_capacity "List of hospitals by capacity") Berlin has a long history of discoveries in medicine and innovations in medical technology.[[201]](#cite_note-202) The modern history of medicine has been significantly influenced by scientists from Berlin. [Rudolf Virchow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudolf_Virchow "Rudolf Virchow") was the founder of cellular pathology, while [Robert Koch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Koch "Robert Koch") developed vaccines for anthrax, cholera, and tuberculosis.[[202]](#cite_note-203) For his life's work Koch is seen as one of the founders of modern medicine.[[203]](#cite_note-204) The [Charité](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charité "Charité") complex (Universitätsklinik Charité) is the largest [university hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_hospital "University hospital") in Europe, tracing back its origins to the year 1710. More than half of all German Nobel Prize winners in Physiology or Medicine, including [Emil von Behring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_von_Behring "Emil von Behring"), Robert Koch and [Paul Ehrlich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Ehrlich "Paul Ehrlich"), have worked at the Charité. The Charité is spread over four campuses and comprises around 3,000 beds, 15,500 staff, 8,000 students, and more than 60 operating theaters, and it has a turnover of two billion euros annually.[[204]](#cite_note-Charité_–_Universitätsmedizin_Berlin-205) ## Education and research [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=41 "Edit section: Education and research")] Main article: [Education in Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_in_Berlin "Education in Berlin") [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Berlin-Mitte_Humboldt-Uni_05-2014.jpg/250px-Berlin-Mitte_Humboldt-Uni_05-2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Berlin-Mitte_Humboldt-Uni_05-2014.jpg) The [Humboldt University of Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humboldt_University_of_Berlin "Humboldt University of Berlin"), the world's first modern university,[[205]](#cite_note-206) is affiliated with 57 Nobel Prize winners. As of 2014[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit), Berlin had 878 schools, teaching 340,658 students in 13,727 classes and 56,787 trainees in businesses and elsewhere.[[146]](#cite_note-berlin.de-147) The city has a 6-year primary education program. After completing primary school, students continue to the *Sekundarschule* (a comprehensive school) or *Gymnasium* (college preparatory school). Berlin has a special bilingual school program in the *Europaschule*, in which children are taught the curriculum in German and a foreign language, starting in primary school and continuing in high school.[[206]](#cite_note-207) The [Französisches Gymnasium Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Französisches_Gymnasium_Berlin "Französisches Gymnasium Berlin"), which was founded in 1689 to teach the children of Huguenot refugees, offers (German/French) instruction.[[207]](#cite_note-208) The [John F. Kennedy School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_School,_Berlin "John F. Kennedy School, Berlin"), a bilingual German–American public school in [Zehlendorf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zehlendorf_(Berlin) "Zehlendorf (Berlin)"), is particularly popular with children of diplomats and the English-speaking expatriate community. 82 *Gymnasien* teach [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin "Latin")[[208]](#cite_note-209) and 8 teach [Classical Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_Greek "Classical Greek").[[209]](#cite_note-210) ### Higher education [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=42 "Edit section: Higher education")] Main article: [Universities and research institutions in Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universities_and_research_institutions_in_Berlin "Universities and research institutions in Berlin") [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Freie_Universitaet_Berlin_-_Gebaeudekomplex_Rost-_und_Silberlaube.jpg/250px-Freie_Universitaet_Berlin_-_Gebaeudekomplex_Rost-_und_Silberlaube.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Freie_Universitaet_Berlin_-_Gebaeudekomplex_Rost-_und_Silberlaube.jpg) The [Free University of Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_University_of_Berlin "Free University of Berlin") The Berlin-Brandenburg capital region is one of the most prolific centers of higher education and research in Germany and Europe. Historically, 67 Nobel Prize winners are affiliated with the Berlin-based universities. The city has four public research universities and more than 30 private, professional, and technical colleges *(Hochschulen)*, offering a wide range of disciplines.[[210]](#cite_note-211) A record number of 175,651 students were enrolled in the winter term of 2015/16.[[211]](#cite_note-212) Among them around 18% have an international background. The three largest universities combined have approximately 103,000 enrolled students. There are the [Freie Universität Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_University_of_Berlin "Free University of Berlin") *(Free University of Berlin, FU Berlin)* with about 33,000[[212]](#cite_note-213) students, the [Humboldt Universität zu Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humboldt_University_of_Berlin "Humboldt University of Berlin") *(HU Berlin)* with 35,000[[213]](#cite_note-214) students, and [Technische Universität Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technische_Universität_Berlin "Technische Universität Berlin") *(TU Berlin)* with 35,000[[214]](#cite_note-215) students. The [Charité](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charité "Charité") Medical School has around 8,000 students.[[204]](#cite_note-Charité_–_Universitätsmedizin_Berlin-205) The FU, the HU, the TU, and the Charité make up the [Berlin University Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_University_Alliance "Berlin University Alliance"), which has received funding from the [Excellence Strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Universities_Excellence_Initiative "German Universities Excellence Initiative") program of the German government.[[215]](#cite_note-216)[[216]](#cite_note-217) The [Universität der Künste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_University_of_the_Arts "Berlin University of the Arts") *(UdK)* has about 4,000 students and [ESMT Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESMT_Berlin "ESMT Berlin") is only one of four business schools in Germany with [triple accreditation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_accreditation "Triple accreditation").[[217]](#cite_note-218) The [Hertie School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertie_School "Hertie School"), a private public policy school located in Mitte, has more than 900 students and doctoral students. The [Berlin School of Economics and Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_School_of_Economics_and_Law "Berlin School of Economics and Law") has an enrollment of about 11,000 students, the [Berlin University of Applied Sciences and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berliner_Hochschule_für_Technik "Berliner Hochschule für Technik") of about 12,000 students, and the [Hochschule für Technik und Wirtschaft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTW_Berlin "HTW Berlin") (University of Applied Sciences for Engineering and Economics) of about 14,000 students. ### Research [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=43 "Edit section: Research")] [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/Berlin_Adlershof_Photonics_Center_2016.jpg/250px-Berlin_Adlershof_Photonics_Center_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Berlin_Adlershof_Photonics_Center_2016.jpg) The [WISTA Science and Technology Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WISTA "WISTA") in [Adlershof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin-Adlershof "Berlin-Adlershof") The city has a high density of internationally renowned research institutions, such as the [Fraunhofer Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraunhofer_Society "Fraunhofer Society"), the [DLR Institute for Planetary Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DLR_Institute_for_Planetary_Research "DLR Institute for Planetary Research"), the [Leibniz Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leibniz_Association "Leibniz Association"), the [Helmholtz Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmholtz_Association_of_German_Research_Centres "Helmholtz Association of German Research Centres"), and the [Max Planck Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Planck_Society "Max Planck Society"), which are independent of, or only loosely connected to its universities.[[218]](#cite_note-219) In 2012, around 65,000 professional scientists were working in [research and development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_and_development "Research and development") in the city.[[146]](#cite_note-berlin.de-147) Berlin is one of the knowledge and innovation communities (KIC) of the [European Institute of Innovation and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Institute_of_Innovation_and_Technology "European Institute of Innovation and Technology") (EIT).[[219]](#cite_note-220) The KIC is based at the Center for Entrepreneurship at TU Berlin and has a focus in the development of IT industries. It partners with major multinational companies such as [Siemens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siemens "Siemens"), [Deutsche Telekom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Telekom "Deutsche Telekom"), and [SAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAP_SE "SAP SE").[[220]](#cite_note-221) One of Europe's successful research, business and technology [clusters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_technology_centers "List of technology centers") is based at [WISTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WISTA "WISTA") in [Berlin-Adlershof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin-Adlershof "Berlin-Adlershof"), with more than 1,000 affiliated firms, university departments and scientific institutions.[[221]](#cite_note-222) In addition to the university-affiliated libraries, the [Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staatsbibliothek_zu_Berlin "Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin") is a major research library. Its two main locations are on Potsdamer Straße and on [Unter den Linden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unter_den_Linden "Unter den Linden"). There are also 86 public libraries in the city.[[146]](#cite_note-berlin.de-147) [ResearchGate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ResearchGate "ResearchGate"), a global social networking site for scientists, is based in Berlin. ## Culture [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=44 "Edit section: Culture")] Main article: [Culture in Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_in_Berlin "Culture in Berlin") [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Alte_Nationalgalerie_abends_%28Zuschnitt%29.jpg/250px-Alte_Nationalgalerie_abends_%28Zuschnitt%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alte_Nationalgalerie_abends_(Zuschnitt).jpg) The [Alte Nationalgalerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alte_Nationalgalerie "Alte Nationalgalerie") is part of the [Museum Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_Island "Museum Island"), a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site "UNESCO World Heritage Site"). Berlin is known for its numerous cultural institutions, many of which enjoy international reputation.[[26]](#cite_note-UNESCO-27)[[222]](#cite_note-UNESCO-2-223) The diversity and vivacity of the metropolis led to a trendsetting atmosphere.[[223]](#cite_note-224) An innovative music, dance and art scene has developed in the 21st century. Young people, international artists and entrepreneurs continued to settle in the city and made Berlin a popular entertainment center in the world.[[224]](#cite_note-225) The expanding cultural performance of the city was underscored by the relocation of the [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group") who decided to move their headquarters to the banks of the River Spree.[[225]](#cite_note-226) In 2005, Berlin was named "City of Design" by [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO") and has been part of the [Creative Cities Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_Cities_Network "Creative Cities Network") ever since.[[226]](#cite_note-227)[[23]](#cite_note-UNESCO-2005-24) ### Galleries and museums [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=45 "Edit section: Galleries and museums")] For a more comprehensive list, see [List of museums and galleries in Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_museums_and_galleries_in_Berlin "List of museums and galleries in Berlin"). [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Nofretete_Neues_Museum.jpg/250px-Nofretete_Neues_Museum.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nofretete_Neues_Museum.jpg) [Thutmose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thutmose_(sculptor) "Thutmose (sculptor)"), *[Bust of Nefertiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bust_of_Nefertiti "Bust of Nefertiti")*, [Egyptian Museum of Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_Museum_of_Berlin "Egyptian Museum of Berlin") As of 2011[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit) Berlin is home to 138 museums and more than 400 art galleries.[[146]](#cite_note-berlin.de-147)[[227]](#cite_note-228) The ensemble on the [Museum Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_Island "Museum Island") is a UNESCO [World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site") and is in the northern part of the Spree Island between the Spree and the Kupfergraben.[[26]](#cite_note-UNESCO-27) As early as 1841 it was designated a "district dedicated to art and antiquities" by a royal decree. Subsequently, the [Altes Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altes_Museum "Altes Museum") was built in the Lustgarten. The [Neues Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neues_Museum "Neues Museum"), which displays the [bust of Queen Nefertiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nefertiti_Bust "Nefertiti Bust"),[[228]](#cite_note-229) [Alte Nationalgalerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alte_Nationalgalerie "Alte Nationalgalerie"), [Pergamon Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pergamon_Museum "Pergamon Museum"), and [Bode Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bode_Museum "Bode Museum") were built there. Apart from the Museum Island, there are many additional museums in the city. The [Gemäldegalerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemäldegalerie,_Berlin "Gemäldegalerie, Berlin") (Painting Gallery) focuses on the paintings of the "old masters" from the 13th to the 18th centuries, while the [Neue Nationalgalerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neue_Nationalgalerie "Neue Nationalgalerie") (New National Gallery, built by [Ludwig Mies van der Rohe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Mies_van_der_Rohe "Ludwig Mies van der Rohe")) specializes in 20th-century European painting. The [Hamburger Bahnhof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburger_Bahnhof "Hamburger Bahnhof"), in [Moabit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moabit "Moabit"), exhibits a major collection of modern and contemporary art. The expanded [Deutsches Historisches Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsches_Historisches_Museum "Deutsches Historisches Museum") reopened in the Zeughaus with an overview of German history spanning more than a millennium. The [Bauhaus Archive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bauhaus_Archive "Bauhaus Archive") is a museum of 20th-century design from the famous [Bauhaus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bauhaus "Bauhaus") school. [Museum Berggruen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_Berggruen "Museum Berggruen") houses the collection of noted 20th century collector [Heinz Berggruen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinz_Berggruen "Heinz Berggruen"), and features an extensive assortment of works by [Picasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picasso "Picasso"), [Matisse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matisse "Matisse"), [Cézanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cézanne "Cézanne"), and [Giacometti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giacometti "Giacometti"), among others.[[229]](#cite_note-230) The [Kupferstichkabinett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kupferstichkabinett_Berlin "Kupferstichkabinett Berlin") Berlin (Museum of Prints and Drawings) is part of the [Staatlichen Museen zu Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_State_Museums "Berlin State Museums") (Berlin State Museums) and the [Kulturforum at Potsdamer Platz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kulturforum "Kulturforum") in the Tiergarten district of Berlin's Mitte district. It is the largest museum of the graphic arts in Germany and at the same time one of the four most important collections of its kind in the world.[[230]](#cite_note-231) The collection includes [Friedrich Gilly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich_Gilly "Friedrich Gilly")'s design for the monument to Frederick II of Prussia.[[231]](#cite_note-232) [![Exterior of Fotografiska Berlin](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Exterior_of_Fotografiska_Berlin.jpg/250px-Exterior_of_Fotografiska_Berlin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Exterior_of_Fotografiska_Berlin.jpg) Exterior of [Fotografiska Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fotografiska "Fotografiska") on Oranienburger Str. Berlin hosts several major institutions dedicated to photography, reflecting the city's historical and contemporary engagement with the medium. The Museum für Fotografie, part of the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and home to the Helmut Newton Foundation, presents historical and contemporary photographic works alongside the permanent exhibition *Helmut Newton's Private Property*. [Fotografiska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fotografiska "Fotografiska") Berlin, opened in 2023 in the [Kunsthaus Tacheles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsthaus_Tacheles "Kunsthaus Tacheles"), focuses on modern and contemporary photography through showcasing local and international photographers alongside public programming. [C/O Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C/O_Berlin "C/O Berlin"), located in the Amerika Haus near [Zoologischer Garten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoologischer_Garten_Berlin "Zoologischer Garten Berlin"), is a leading exhibition space for photography and visual media, known for showcasing both established and emerging photographers. Photography also plays a significant role within broader institutions such as the [Berlinische Galerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlinische_Galerie "Berlinische Galerie"), which integrates photography into its presentation of modern art, and the [Kunstbibliothek Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunstbibliothek_Berlin "Kunstbibliothek Berlin"), which holds an extensive photographic archive. Additional venues such as the [Friedrichshain Photo Gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrichshain_Photo_Gallery "Friedrichshain Photo Gallery") contribute to the city's documentary and socially engaged photographic culture. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/Ishtar_Gate_at_Berlin_Museum.jpg/250px-Ishtar_Gate_at_Berlin_Museum.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ishtar_Gate_at_Berlin_Museum.jpg) The reconstructed [Ishtar Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ishtar_Gate "Ishtar Gate") of Babylon at the [Pergamon Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pergamon_Museum "Pergamon Museum") [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/JewishMuseumBerlin.jpg/250px-JewishMuseumBerlin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JewishMuseumBerlin.jpg) The [Jewish Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Museum_Berlin "Jewish Museum Berlin") presents two millennia of [German–Jewish history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Jews "German Jews"). The [Jewish Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Museum_Berlin "Jewish Museum Berlin") has a standing exhibition on two millennia of German-Jewish history.[[232]](#cite_note-233) The [German Museum of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Museum_of_Technology_(Berlin) "German Museum of Technology (Berlin)") in [Kreuzberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kreuzberg "Kreuzberg") has a large collection of historical technical artifacts. The *[Museum für Naturkunde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_History_Museum,_Berlin "Natural History Museum, Berlin")* (Berlin's [natural history museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_history_museum "Natural history museum")) exhibits [natural history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_history "Natural history") near [Berlin Hauptbahnhof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Hauptbahnhof "Berlin Hauptbahnhof"). It has the largest mounted dinosaur in the world (a *[Giraffatitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giraffatitan "Giraffatitan")* skeleton). A well-preserved specimen of *[Tyrannosaurus rex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrannosaurus "Tyrannosaurus")* and the early bird *[Archaeopteryx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaeopteryx "Archaeopteryx")* are at display as well.[[233]](#cite_note-234) In [Dahlem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dahlem_(Berlin) "Dahlem (Berlin)"), there are several museums of world art and culture, such as the [Museum of Asian Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Asian_Art "Museum of Asian Art"), the [Ethnological Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnological_Museum_of_Berlin "Ethnological Museum of Berlin"), the [Museum of European Cultures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_Europäischer_Kulturen "Museum Europäischer Kulturen"), as well as the [Allied Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied_Museum "Allied Museum"). The [Brücke Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brücke_Museum "Brücke Museum") features one of the largest collection of works by artist of the early 20th-century expressionist movement. In [Lichtenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lichtenberg,_Berlin "Lichtenberg, Berlin"), on the grounds of the former [East German Ministry for State Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stasi "Stasi"), is the [Stasi Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stasi_Museum "Stasi Museum"). The site of [Checkpoint Charlie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Checkpoint_Charlie "Checkpoint Charlie"), one of the most renowned crossing points of the Berlin Wall, is still preserved. A private [museum venture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Checkpoint_Charlie_Museum "Checkpoint Charlie Museum") exhibits a comprehensive documentation of detailed plans and strategies devised by people who tried to flee from the East. The [Beate Uhse Erotic Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beate_Uhse_Erotic_Museum "Beate Uhse Erotic Museum") claimed to be the largest erotic museum in the world until it closed in 2014.[[234]](#cite_note-235)[[235]](#cite_note-236) The cityscape of Berlin displays large quantities of urban [street art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_art "Street art").[[236]](#cite_note-237) It has become a significant part of the city's cultural heritage and has its roots in the graffiti scene of [Kreuzberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kreuzberg "Kreuzberg") of the 1980s.[[237]](#cite_note-238) The [Berlin Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Wall_graffiti_art "Berlin Wall graffiti art") itself has become one of the largest open-air canvasses in the world.[[238]](#cite_note-239) The leftover stretch along the Spree river in [Friedrichshain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrichshain "Friedrichshain") remains as the [East Side Gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Side_Gallery "East Side Gallery"). Berlin today is consistently rated as an important world city for street art culture.[[239]](#cite_note-240) Berlin has galleries which are quite rich in contemporary art. Located in Mitte, KW Institute for Contemporary Art, KOW, Sprüth Magers; Kreuzberg there are a few galleries as well such as Blain Southern, [Esther Schipper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esther_Schipper "Esther Schipper"), Future Gallery, König Gallerie. ### Nightlife and festivals [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=46 "Edit section: Nightlife and festivals")] Berlin's nightlife has been celebrated as one of the most diverse and vibrant of its kind.[[240]](#cite_note-241)[[241]](#cite_note-242) In the 1970s and 80s, the [SO36](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SO36 "SO36") in [Kreuzberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kreuzberg "Kreuzberg") was a center for [punk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_music "Punk music") and culture. The *SOUND* and the *Dschungel* gained notoriety. Throughout the 1990s, people in their 20s from all over the world, particularly those in [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Europe "Western Europe") and Central Europe, made Berlin's club scene a premier nightlife venue. After the [fall of the Berlin Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Berlin_Wall "Fall of the Berlin Wall") in 1989, many historic buildings in Mitte, the former city center of East Berlin, were illegally occupied and re-built by young squatters and became a fertile ground for underground and [counterculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counterculture "Counterculture") gatherings.[[242]](#cite_note-243) The central boroughs are home to many nightclubs, including the [Tresor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tresor_(club) "Tresor (club)") and the [Berghain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berghain "Berghain"). The [KitKatClub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KitKatClub "KitKatClub") and several other locations are known for their sexually uninhibited parties. Clubs are not required to close at a fixed time during the weekends, and many parties last well into the morning or even all weekend, including near [Alexanderplatz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexanderplatz "Alexanderplatz"). Several venues have become a popular stage for the [Neo-Burlesque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Burlesque "Neo-Burlesque") scene. Berlin has a long history of gay culture, and is an important [birthplace of the LGBT rights movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific-Humanitarian_Committee "Scientific-Humanitarian Committee"). Same-sex bars and dance halls operated freely as early as the 1880s, and the first gay magazine, *[Der Eigene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Der_Eigene "Der Eigene")*, started in 1896. By the 1920s, gays and lesbians had an unprecedented visibility.[[243]](#cite_note-244)[[244]](#cite_note-245) Today, in addition to a positive atmosphere in the wider club scene, the city again has a huge number of queer clubs and festivals. The most famous and largest are [Berlin Pride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Pride "Berlin Pride"), the [Christopher Street Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Street_Day "Christopher Street Day"),[[245]](#cite_note-246) the [Lesbian and Gay City Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesbian_and_Gay_City_Festival "Lesbian and Gay City Festival") in Berlin-Schöneberg, the [Kreuzberg Pride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kreuzberg_Pride "Kreuzberg Pride"). The annual [Berlin International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_International_Film_Festival "Berlin International Film Festival") (Berlinale) with around 500,000 admissions is considered to be the largest publicly attended film festival in the world.[[246]](#cite_note-247)[[247]](#cite_note-248) The Karneval der Kulturen (*Carnival of Cultures*), a multi-ethnic street parade, is celebrated every [Pentecost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentecost "Pentecost") weekend.[[248]](#cite_note-249) Berlin is also well known for the cultural festival [Berliner Festspiele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berliner_Festspiele "Berliner Festspiele"), which includes the jazz festival [JazzFest Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JazzFest_Berlin "JazzFest Berlin"), and [Young Euro Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Euro_Classic "Young Euro Classic"), the largest international festival of [youth orchestras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youth_orchestra "Youth orchestra") in the world. Several technology and media art festivals and conferences are held in the city, including [Transmediale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmediale "Transmediale") and [Chaos Communication Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaos_Communication_Congress "Chaos Communication Congress"). The annual [Berlin Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Festival "Berlin Festival") focuses on indie rock, electronic music and synthpop and is part of the International Berlin Music Week.[[249]](#cite_note-250)[[250]](#cite_note-251) Every year Berlin hosts one of the largest New Year's Eve celebrations in the world, attended by well over a million people. The focal point is the Brandenburg Gate, where midnight fireworks are centered, but various private fireworks displays take place throughout the entire city.
