Sir [Simon Rattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Rattle "Simon Rattle") conducting the renowned [Berlin Philharmonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Philharmonic "Berlin Philharmonic") Berlin is home to 44 theaters and stages.[[146]](#cite_note-berlin.de-147) The [Deutsches Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsches_Theater_(Berlin) "Deutsches Theater (Berlin)") in Mitte was built in 1849–50 and has operated almost continuously since then. The [Volksbühne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volksbühne "Volksbühne") at [Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz "Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz") was built in 1913–14, though the company had been founded in 1890. The [Berliner Ensemble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berliner_Ensemble "Berliner Ensemble"), famous for performing the works of [Bertolt Brecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertolt_Brecht "Bertolt Brecht"), was established in 1949. The [Schaubühne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schaubühne "Schaubühne") was founded in 1962 and moved to the building of the former Universum Cinema on Kurfürstendamm in 1981. With a [seating capacity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seating_capacity "Seating capacity") of 1,895 and a stage floor of 2,854 square meters (30,720 sq ft), the [Friedrichstadt-Palast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrichstadt-Palast "Friedrichstadt-Palast") in Berlin Mitte is the largest show palace in Europe. For Berlin's independent dance and theatre scene, venues such as the Sophiensäle in Mitte and the three houses of the [Hebbel am Ufer (HAU)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebbel-Theater "Hebbel-Theater") in Kreuzberg are important. Most productions there are also accessible to an English-speaking audience. Some of the dance and theatre groups that also work internationally ([Gob Squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gob_Squad "Gob Squad"), [Rimini Protokoll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rimini_Protokoll "Rimini Protokoll")) are based there, as well as festivals such as the international festival [Dance in August](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanz_im_August "Tanz im August"). Berlin has three [opera houses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opera_house "Opera house"): the [Deutsche Oper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Oper "Deutsche Oper"), the [Berlin State Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_State_Opera "Berlin State Opera"), and the [Komische Oper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komische_Oper "Komische Oper"). The Berlin State Opera on [Unter den Linden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unter_den_Linden "Unter den Linden") opened in 1742 and is the oldest of the three. Its musical director is [Daniel Barenboim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Barenboim "Daniel Barenboim"). The Komische Oper has traditionally specialized in [operettas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operetta "Operetta") and is also at Unter den Linden. The Deutsche Oper opened in 1912 in Charlottenburg. The city's main venue for musical theater performances are the Theater am Potsdamer Platz and [Theater des Westens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theater_des_Westens "Theater des Westens") (built in 1895). Contemporary dance can be seen at the *Radialsystem V*. The [Tempodrom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempodrom "Tempodrom") is host to concerts and circus-inspired entertainment. It also houses a multi-sensory spa experience. The [Admiralspalast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admiralspalast "Admiralspalast") in Mitte has a vibrant program of variety and music events. There are seven symphony orchestras in Berlin. The [Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Philharmonic_Orchestra "Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra") is one of the preeminent orchestras in the world;[[251]](#cite_note-252) it is housed in the [Berliner Philharmonie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berliner_Philharmonie "Berliner Philharmonie") near Potsdamer Platz on a street named for the orchestra's longest-serving conductor, [Herbert von Karajan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_von_Karajan "Herbert von Karajan").[[252]](#cite_note-253) [Simon Rattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Rattle "Simon Rattle") was its principal conductor from 1999 to 2018, a position now held by [Kirill Petrenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirill_Petrenko "Kirill Petrenko"). The [Konzerthausorchester Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konzerthausorchester_Berlin "Konzerthausorchester Berlin") was founded in 1952 as the orchestra for East Berlin. [Christoph Eschenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christoph_Eschenbach "Christoph Eschenbach") is its principal conductor. The [Haus der Kulturen der Welt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haus_der_Kulturen_der_Welt "Haus der Kulturen der Welt") presents exhibitions dealing with intercultural issues and stages world music and conferences.[[253]](#cite_note-254) The *Kookaburra* and the *Quatsch Comedy Club* are known for satire and comedy shows. In 2018, the *[New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* described Berlin as "arguably the world capital of underground [electronic music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music")".[[254]](#cite_note-255) ### Cuisine [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=48 "Edit section: Cuisine")] Main article: [Cuisine of Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuisine_of_Berlin "Cuisine of Berlin") [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/D%C3%B6ner_Kebab.jpg/250px-D%C3%B6ner_Kebab.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Döner_Kebab.jpg) [Döner kebab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doner_kebab "Doner kebab") [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/Currywurst-1.jpg/250px-Currywurst-1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Currywurst-1.jpg) A plate of [Currywurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Currywurst "Currywurst") Invented in Berlin, currywurst and modern döner are icons of German popular culture and cuisine. The [cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_cuisine "German cuisine") and culinary offerings of Berlin vary greatly. 23 restaurants in Berlin have been awarded one or more [Michelin stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelin_Guide#Stars "Michelin Guide") in the [Michelin Guide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelin_Guide "Michelin Guide") of 2021, which ranks the city at the top for the number of restaurants having this distinction in Germany.[[255]](#cite_note-256) Berlin is well known for its offerings of vegetarian[[256]](#cite_note-257) and [vegan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veganism "Veganism")[[257]](#cite_note-258) cuisine and is home to an innovative entrepreneurial food scene promoting cosmopolitan flavors, local and sustainable ingredients, pop-up street food markets, supper clubs, as well as food festivals, such as Berlin Food Week.[[258]](#cite_note-259)[[259]](#cite_note-260) Many local foods originated from north German culinary traditions and include rustic and hearty dishes with pork, goose, fish, peas, beans, cucumbers, or potatoes. Typical Berliner fare include popular [street food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_food "Street food") like the *[Currywurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Currywurst "Currywurst")* (which gained popularity with postwar construction workers rebuilding the city), *[Buletten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frikadeller "Frikadeller")* and the *[Berliner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berliner_(doughnut) "Berliner (doughnut)")* donut, known in Berlin as *Pfannkuchen* (German: [[ˈp͡fanˌkuːxn̩]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Standard_German "Help:IPA/Standard German") [ⓘ](/wiki/File:De-Pfannkuchen.ogg "File:De-Pfannkuchen.ogg")).[[260]](#cite_note-261)[[261]](#cite_note-262) German bakeries offering a variety of breads and pastries are widespread. One of Europe's largest [delicatessen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delicatessen "Delicatessen") markets is found at the [KaDeWe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KaDeWe "KaDeWe"), and among the world's largest chocolate stores is *Rausch*.[[262]](#cite_note-263)[[263]](#cite_note-264) Berlin is also home to a diverse gastronomy scene reflecting the immigrant history of the city. Turkish and Arab immigrants brought their culinary traditions to the city, such as the [lahmacun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahmacun "Lahmacun") and [falafel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falafel "Falafel"), which have become common fast food staples. The modern fast-food version of the [doner kebab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doner_kebab "Doner kebab") sandwich which [evolved in Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kadir_Nurman "Kadir Nurman") in the 1970s, has since become a favorite dish in Germany and elsewhere in the world.[[264]](#cite_note-265) Asian cuisine like Chinese, Vietnamese, Thai, Indian, Korean, and Japanese restaurants, as well as Spanish tapas bars, Italian, and Greek cuisine, can be found in many parts of the city. ### Recreation [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Berlin&action=edit&section=49 "Edit section: Recreation")] [Zoologischer Garten Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Zoological_Garden "Berlin Zoological Garden"), the older of two zoos in the city, was founded in 1844. It is the most visited zoo in Europe and presents the most diverse range of species in the world.[[265]](#cite_note-266) It was the home of the captive-born celebrity polar bear [Knut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knut_(polar_bear) "Knut (polar bear)").[[266]](#cite_note-267) The city's other zoo, [Tierpark Friedrichsfelde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tierpark_Berlin "Tierpark Berlin"), was founded in 1955. [Berlin's Botanischer Garten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin-Dahlem_Botanical_Garden_and_Botanical_Museum "Berlin-Dahlem Botanical Garden and Botanical Museum") includes the Botanic Museum Berlin. With an area of 43 hectares (110 acres) and around 22,000 different plant species, it is one of the largest and most diverse collections of botanical life in the world. Other gardens in the city include the [Britzer Garten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britzer_Garten "Britzer Garten"), and the [Gärten der Welt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erholungspark_Marzahn "Erholungspark Marzahn") (Gardens of the World) in Marzahn.[[267]](#cite_note-268) The [Tiergarten park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiergarten_(park) "Tiergarten (park)") in Mitte, with landscape design by [Peter Joseph Lenné](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Joseph_Lenné "Peter Joseph Lenné"), is one of Berlin's largest and most popular parks.[[268]](#cite_note-269) In Kreuzberg, the [Viktoriapark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktoriapark "Viktoriapark") provides a viewing point over the southern part of inner-city Berlin. [Treptower Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treptower_Park "Treptower Park"), beside the Spree in [Treptow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treptow "Treptow"), features a large [Soviet War Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_War_Memorial_(Treptower_Park) "Soviet War Memorial (Treptower Park)"). The Volkspark in [Friedrichshain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrichshain "Friedrichshain"), which opened in 1848, is the oldest park in the city, with monuments, a summer outdoor cinema and several sports areas.[[269]](#cite_note-270) [Tempelhofer Feld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempelhofer_Feld "Tempelhofer Feld"), the site of the former [city airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Tempelhof_Airport "Berlin Tempelhof Airport"), is the world's largest inner-city open space.[[270]](#cite_note-271) [Potsdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potsdam "Potsdam") is on the southwestern periphery of Berlin. The city was a residence of the [Prussian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prussia "Prussia") kings and the [German Kaiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Emperor "German Emperor") until 1918. The area around Potsdam, in particular [Sanssouci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanssouci "Sanssouci"), is known for a series of interconnected lakes and cultural landmarks. The [Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palaces_and_Parks_of_Potsdam_and_Berlin "Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin") are the largest [World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site") in Germany.[[222]](#cite_note-UNESCO-2-223) Berlin is also well known for its numerous cafés, street musicians, beach In 2015 Berlin was the venue for the [UEFA Champions League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2015 UEFA Champions League Final"). The city bid to host the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") but lost to [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney").[[276]](#cite_note-277) Berlin hosted the [2023 Special Olympics World Summer Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Special_Olympics_World_Summer_Games "2023 Special Olympics World Summer Games"). This is the first time Germany has ever hosted the Special Olympics World Games.[[277]](#cite_note-278) The annual [Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Marathon "Berlin Marathon") – a course that holds the most top-10 world record runs – and the [ISTAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internationales_Stadionfest "Internationales Stadionfest") are well-established athletic events in the city.[[278]](#cite_note-279) The [Mellowpark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mellowpark "Mellowpark") in Köpenick is one of the biggest skate and BMX parks in Europe.[[279]](#cite_note-280) A fan fest at Brandenburg Gate, which attracts several hundreds of thousands of spectators, has become popular during international football competitions, such as the [UEFA European of modern [sports clubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_clubs "Sports clubs").[[284]](#cite_note-285) In 2013, around 600,000 Berliners were registered in one of the more than 2,300 sport and fitness clubs.[[285]](#cite_note-286) The city of Berlin operates more than 60 public indoor and outdoor swimming pools.[[286]](#cite_note-287) Berlin is the largest Olympic training center in Germany, with around 500 top athletes (15% of all German top athletes) being based there. 47 elite athletes participated in the 2012 Summer Olympics. Berliners would achieve 7 gold, 12 silver, and 3 bronze medals.[[287]](#cite_note-288) Several professional clubs representing the most important spectator team sports in Germany are based in Berlin.
